reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Ok, so perhaps I just wasn't in the mood but this just didn't make me laugh. It's nothing whatsoever to do with the band "Nirvana" - just in case you were wondering. Instead it follows two friends whose dream of playing at the legendary Rivoli club never seems to get any nearer. Perhaps that's because they have no musical talent at all? Well we never find out, but what we do know is that Jay McCarrol is an OK pianist and his pal Matt Johnson is a loud and irritating character who constantly comes up with schemes to secure their success. They've been trying since 2008 and it's the idea of going back in time that appeals to Matt. Determined to manufacture his own flux capacitor to install in their mobile home, he is convinced that's their best plan. Jay, on the other hand, concludes that he'd be much better off on his own and so sets off for an open mike night in not-so-nearby Ottawa. He doesn't realise that his pal is sleeping in the vehicle and so at 88kph, lightning strikes à la "Back to the Future" (1985) and they end up in 2008. Now there, their only wish is to get straight back home, but they mustn't be seen (think Prime Directive sort of thing) as they return to their former flat to procure some fuel. It's now that they have a bit of a domestic and split up - only for their timelines to separate and for Jay to become an international rock star whilst Matt achieves, well, nothing really. Is there any chance the two can be reconciled - in this or any other timeline? Might their friendship endure or will Jay just bin his exasperating floppy-hatted friend and enjoy the fruits of his success? There is a relentless flow of dialogue - usually from a Johnson who clearly thinks that expletives substitute for wit; there's virtually no music to speak of and by mid way through I was expecting Laurel and Hardy to come out with a plank and a bucket. It's all just so predicable and the deliberately visible presence of the camera crews, and what looks like some bemused audience participation, robs us of any chance to buy into any of the sci-fi elements of this increasingly lacklustre story. It's busy and frenetic and if you like zany, then maybe you'll take more from this than I did. I don’t really, and I didn't.

reviews.author: The Fixate & Binge Podcast, w/ Joe Curdy
reviews.content:
Whatever I was expecting — and I went into this as blind as I could — I wasn't anticipating having my jaw on the floor as often as I did. Not since **BEING JOHN MALKOVICH** has a film so thoroughly taken me on a wild ride through surrealism, humor, and gonzo filmmaking that shatters the fourth wall over and over and over again.

Any attempt to explain what happens in the film would spoil the experience — so I'll keep this as vague as possible.

Longtime writers and Canadian comedy duo Matt Johnson and Jay McCarrol play fictionalized versions of themselves in this time-traveling quest for their musical group, Nirvana the Band, to achieve success.

A series of outrageous stunts designed to generate the buzz that will turn heads results in a metaphysical anomaly that bends our perception of time, thrusting both Johnson and McCarrol into a reality that feels like wandering through a traveling carnival's House of Mirrors.

With Christopher "**Tenet**" Nolan-esque "how did they do that?" moments throughout, the film never forgets its purpose: friendship and loyalty, even if the road taken to get there is as bonkers as a Hunter S. Thompson acid trip.

One of the year's biggest surprises, **NIRVANA THE BAND THE SHOW THE MOVIE** offers viewers an experience that can't be matched. Also directed by Johnson (who co-starred and directed the critically-overlooked 2023 film **BLACKBERRY**) -- don't miss the film, streaming now on VOD.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When their latest scheme to secure a gig at Toronto's Rivoli goes wildly off course, indie musicians Matt and Jay accidentally build a working time machine and travel back to 2008.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Frustrated after years of failed publicity stunts, Toronto indie music duo Matt and Jay attempt an ambitious new ploy to book a show at the iconic Rivoli venue. Their plan takes an unexpected turn when a fake time machine attached to their RV actually works, transporting the pair back to the year 2008. While stranded in the past, their unintentional meddling alters their own history, forcing them to navigate a drastically altered present timeline. To restore their original lives, the duo must race against time to fix the past before their future is permanently ruined.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Fictionalized versions of musicians Matt Johnson and Jay McCarrol have spent seventeen years devising absurd publicity stunts in an ongoing effort to book a show at Toronto's Rivoli. When Matt concocts a dramatic skydiving scheme that goes disastrously wrong, Jay secretly tries to pursue a solo path, straining their friendship. Desperate to keep the band together, Matt installs a homage time machine onto their RV, unaware that an accidental combination of ingredients will cause it to function. The pair is suddenly catapulted back to 2008, landing right in the middle of their younger selves' early band days. While attempting to secure supplies to return home, Matt and Jay inadvertently interact with their past selves and alter their whiteboard plans. Returning to the present, they discover a altered reality where Jay is a successful solo artist and Matt is reduced to playing in a cover band. As Jay's new life spiraling into chaos forces him to seek Matt's help, the two realize they must harness a massive surge of electricity to power the RV once again. Working together against law enforcement and severe weather, they attempt to tap into a lightning strike at the CN Tower to re-establish the timeline. Ultimately, their chaotic journey forces both men to confront their deep-seated insecurities, creative differences, and enduring bond.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie follows the chaotic misadventures of Matt and Jay, two delusionally ambitious musicians in Toronto who have spent nearly two decades trying to book a single performance at the Rivoli. When their latest extravagant publicity scheme fails, a bizarre mishap accidentally turns their makeshift RV into a functional time machine, hurtling the duo back to the year 2008. Facing the bizarre reality of their past lives, Matt and Jay must navigate nostalgia, unintended timeline changes, and their own precarious friendship as they search for a way back to the present without destroying their future.

faq.answer: Yes. The film is part of a franchise based on the 2007–2009 web series 'Nirvana the Band the Show' and its 2017–2018 television series adaptation of the same name.
faq.question: Is this movie part of a franchise?

faq.answer: Yes, the film features a post-credits scene that expands on the time-travel narrative and connects directly back to the timeline of the series.
faq.question: Is there a post-credit scene?

faq.answer: The dominant genre is comedy, specifically blending mockumentary, satire, sci-fi time travel, and guerrilla-style improvisational filmmaking.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre?

faq.answer: The story follows musical duo Matt and Jay whose latest harebrained scheme to book a gig at Toronto's Rivoli venue goes disastrously wrong, accidentally sending them back in time to 2008.
faq.question: What is the basic plot of Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie?

faq.answer: The movie stars creators Matt Johnson and Jay McCarrol, who play fictionalized, bumbling versions of themselves.
faq.question: Who stars in the movie?

faq.answer: The film was directed by Matt Johnson, who also co-wrote the screenplay alongside Jay McCarrol.
faq.question: Who directed Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie?

faq.answer: No. While long-time fans will appreciate inside jokes and callbacks, the movie was specifically crafted to be fully enjoyable for newcomers with no prior context.
faq.question: Do I need to watch the TV series before watching the movie?

faq.answer: The film was shot on location in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, featuring iconic real-world locations such as the Rivoli and the CN Tower.
faq.question: Where was the movie filmed?
